concept.name: Sign of strength
concept.definition: The Wyckoff event (SOS) in which price advances on widening spread and relatively higher volume, showing demand in control; after accumulation, it often validates the preceding spring or test and typically carries price to or through the top of the trading range.
concept.intuition: The first rally with real conviction behind it, proving buyers have taken the wheel.
concept.mechanics: The analyst looks for rallies whose price bars widen in spread with expanding volume, in contrast to the narrowing, low-volume reactions of the range. An SOS following a spring confirms the bullish reading; a decisive SOS that crosses the range's resistance is called a 'jump across the creek'.
concept.failure_modes: A single strong bar can be an upthrust or a news-driven spike rather than genuine demand; an SOS that fails to hold its gains and falls back into the range negates the confirmation.
concept.misconceptions: An SOS is not simply 'a big green bar'; its meaning comes from context — appearing after accumulation events and being followed by shallow, low-volume reactions (LPSs).
concept.example: Following a spring at 87, a stock rallies from 91 to 104 on expanding volume and wide daily ranges, punching through the range top; the analyst labels the move an SOS and looks for a low-volume pullback to enter.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
